note: Two north and east Bengal folk forms under one name: bhawaiya (cart-driver and buffalo-herder songs with dotara, from Rangpur and Cooch Behar) and bhatiali (slow river songs of the boatmen). Bengali titles have no single romanisation, so they are spelled as each release spells them.

size.basis: No source counts recordings. Recording began on 78s in Kolkata in the 1930s–40s (Abbasuddin Ahmed for HMV, Megaphone, Twin and Regal; Kamala Jharia's 1934 bhatiali side), then decades of radio (Bangladesh Betar, All India Radio) and cassette releases on both sides of the border, and a large current stream of singles: an iTunes search finds 36 albums and singles titled 'bhawaiya' and 24 'bhatiali' (most since 2015), plus label series such as banglanatak's Bhawaiya and Bhatiyali VOL 1–3 (16–17 tracks each). One major folk singer, Abdul Alim, recorded about 500 songs across all folk forms. The canon an insider would name is a few dozen songs (oki gariyal bhai, fande pariya baga kande re, amay bhashaili re, etc.) in versions by Abbasuddin, his children, Rathindranath Roy and a handful of others.
